net_change: The shorter hip-to-ankle interval and added leg channels make the lower frame read less like long thin sticks, and the narrower upper body is modestly less barrel-like from the front. The extended head position gives the neck more presence. I do not see a gross loss of torso or leg mass: the chest stays full and the legs retain their articulated load path, though the shortened legs now risk looking slightly compressed relative to the long exposed legs in the owner image.

prioritized_remaining_fixes.finding: The owner reference carries the head through a curved throat into a forward-full chest that narrows toward a visible dark leg-root frame. Frame03 still reads as a straight upright neck joint above one smooth egg/barrel torso, with little breast-to-pelvis transition. The new neck height has not yet made the S-curve; the head and shoulder mantle still feel perched apart from the torso.
prioritized_remaining_fixes.direction: Shape one continuous forward throat and chest contour, then taper the underside into a leg-root/pelvic frame; preserve chest fullness while avoiding another uniform barrel or stacked collar.

prioritized_remaining_fixes.finding: The leg channels improve visible structural mass over V21, but the hip-to-ankle shortening makes the articulated limbs look more compressed. The reference keeps substantial exposed leg length below the breast and resolves it into long, grounded feet.
prioritized_remaining_fixes.direction: Keep the channels and bearing transitions, but reassess the shortened upper leg interval against the whole-body side silhouette before reducing it further; maintain a readable exposed thigh/shank path and grounded toe reach.

perspective_limit: The owner image is a dramatic perspective illustration; these are comparative silhouette judgments, not calibrated dimensions or exact proportion measurements.
acceptance: This review is not owner likeness acceptance, runtime validation, or clearance evidence.
